body:
# the contributor audit: seven-fiber total-density envelope obstruction

Source: `candidate b04c74715df6cea2`.

The accompanying exact verifier was rerun successfully (2,570 checks).

The universal envelope beta is an infimum at the prescribed centroid of
1_F+2eta. It is not the best depth of 1_F+eta over arbitrary centers.
Its upper bounds require only explicit admissible witnesses, so no
attainment of this infimum is assumed. Uniform eta=alpha*1_F on a
simplex gives beta<=Gamma_d(1+alpha) for all L>=alpha.

For the planar two-band witness, the rank v=(1-x)^2 is uniform. The
two density-L bands have exactly the claimed masses r and alpha-r and
remain in [0,1], disjoint up to endpoints, on all three closed cells.
The tested cap x>=1/3 has raw auxiliary mass 4/9+4/25=136/225.
Its containing the specified centroid is equivalent to the displayed
square-root moment inequality. Direct integration gives

  (alpha+8L/27)*sqrt(L) >= 8/125+(alpha+4L/9-4/25)^(3/2).

The auxiliary C and P quantities in the source give a sufficient strict
inequality with the correct sign on both squarings. Their printed
Bernstein coefficients are all positive; expansion in the verifier
confirms the exact polynomial identities, including all cell endpoints.
The witness is admissible for any larger ceiling, so the minimum-ceiling
allocation comparison has the correct direction.

The double-cone convex hull has exactly the fibers asserted: total apex
weight is at least |z|/4, and the copies contracted toward a contained
vertex are nested. Truncation to [-3,3] gives precisely seven positive
integer fibers, original mass 11/4, and nonaffine centroid graph. At
the central base, fractional knapsack minimizes the sum density ceiling
by filling the three pair capacities in decreasing order. This yields
exactly the three-cell L_min and exhausts every allocation. At the other
bases, each pair's smaller endpoint is the one farther from zero, giving
k+T<=7/8. The original denominator is never replaced by allocated mass.

Binary padding creates no cross-block reflected pairs at an integer
anchor: a midpoint in {0,1} forces both endpoint bits equal to that bit.
It multiplies total mass by 2^(n-1), leaving the OC raw target 11/18.
Thus the certificate bound 136/225 has the stated gap 1/150 in every n.

Finally, the actual source (0,P/4) is safe independently: the identical
neighbor copies each have volume 9/16 and centroid P/4; the own triangle
contains a further identical copy. The proved paired-tail inequality
pays 2Gamma_2 times that volume on the two neighbors, and ordinary
Grunbaum pays another Gamma_2 times it on the own copy. Their sum is
3/4>11/18. Integer-only normals and containing rather than through-source
caps are separately valid. Other binary blocks can only add mass.

Accordingly this is not an OC counterexample. The two-band witness need
not be an actual midpoint law of the chain. The result excludes only
universal guarantees that forget geometry beyond total midpoint mass
and total density ceiling at the specified centroid.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
